title: Poor engine condition caused Colombo-KKS train breakdown: Deputy Minister
byline: The poor condition of the engine caused the breakdown of the Colombo-Kankesanthurai (KKS) train yesterday (20), Deputy Minister of Transport Prasanna Gunasena told Parliament.

title: Parliament pays tribute to late singer Nanda Malini
byline: Parliament today paid tribute to late veteran singer Nanda Malini, recalling her immense contribution to Sri Lankan music and society.

title: Namal appears before Police FCID
byline: Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa arrived at the Police Financial Crimes Investigation Division (FCID) this morning in response to a summons issued in connection with an ongoing investigation.

title: Castlereagh and Maussakelle reservoirs reach overflow levels
byline: Water levels in the Castlereagh and Maussakelle reservoirs have reached their respective overflow levels following intermittent rainfall in the surrounding catchment areas, officials said.

title: US Ambassador-designate meets Sri Lanka’s Charge d’Affaires
byline: United States Ambassador-designate to Sri Lanka Eric Meyer met Sri Lanka’s Charge d’Affaires in Washington D.C. yesterday (August 20), ahead of his departure for Sri Lanka.

title: PHIs go on sick leave today over transfer
byline: Public Health Inspectors (PHIs) across the country have reported sick leave today as part of an islandwide symbolic trade union action over the transfer of a PHI attached to the Health Office at the Bandaranaike International Airport in Katunayake.

title: Police clearance service hit by system outage
byline: The Sri Lanka Police has temporarily suspended the submission of applications for police clearance certificates due to a technical issue affecting its computerized data system.

title: Programme planned to certify chemical-free fruits
byline: The Government is planning to introduce a certification programme to ensure that fruits sold in the local market are free from harmful chemical residues, while measures are also being considered to promote safe fruit-ripening practices.

title: Tipper-tractor crash claims five lives in Monaragala
byline: Five people have died following a serious road accident in the Kumbukkan area of Monaragala early this morning (21), police said.

title: Gazette notification on deploying elephants for Peraheras soon
byline: The Environment Ministry is preparing to issue a Gazette notification establishing a mechanism to regulate and deploy captive elephants for Peraheras and other cultural and religious events, following Cabinet approval for the initiative

title: Sri Lankan star emerges as Chopra’s biggest threat
byline: Neeraj Chopra will face a reshuffled javelin field at the Lausanne Diamond League on Friday night, with Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage emerging as one of the leading challengers following Julian Weber’s withdrawal.

title: Bangladesh elects ruling party veteran Alamgir as president
byline: Bangladeshi lawmakers elected veteran Bangladesh Nationalist Party leader Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir as the country’s new president on Thursday, making the longtime opposition figure the head of state after his party came to power in a major political transition.

title: 2027 school term dates and exam schedule announced
byline: The Ministry of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education has issued Circular No. 31/2026 outlining the school term schedule, public holiday calendar and major examination dates for 2027.

title: Sri Lanka targets full digital ID implementation by August 2027
byline: ​Sri Lanka is set to issue its first National Digital Identity (Digital ID) this year, with nationwide implementation targeted for completion by August 2027, unlocking a strategic digitalization initiative that has remained stalled for over a decade.

title: Emergency airlift planned as Filgrastim shortage hits hospitals
byline: A Daily Mirror report on the shortage of the cancer drug Filgrastim, published on August 18 under the headline “Drug shortage puts cancer patients’ lives at stake,” came under scrutiny in Parliament yesterday, with MP Shanakiyan Rasamanickam questioning Health Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa over the issue.

title: Sri Lanka becomes new transshipment hub for Lamborghinis
byline: Sri Lanka’s Hambantota International Port has become an important transit point for luxury vehicles including Lamborghinis as the Middle East conflict continues to disrupt shipping routes around the Strait of Hormuz.

title: High Court acquits technical officer in Rs. 40,000 bribery case
byline: The Colombo High Court today acquitted a Technical Officer who had been charged with soliciting a bribe of Rs. 40,000 on two occasions and accepting a total of Rs. 40,000 in two instalments of Rs. 20,000 each.

title: Fake banker, big food order, then theft: Police hunt suspect
byline: The Police are seeking public assistance to identify and apprehend a suspect allegedly involved in a series of fraudulent activities and thefts targeting hotels and commercial establishments.

title: Parliament approves Rs. 7.5 Billion supplementary estimate for Yala paddy purchases
byline: The Supplementary Estimate to provide Rs. 7500 million required by the government to purchase paddy from the 2026 Yala season was approved by Parliament today.

title: Namal leaves FCID after six-hour statement
byline: Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa left the Police Financial Crimes Investigation Division (FCID) today after recording a statement for nearly six hours.

title: Iran vows ’devastating’ response as US threatens toughest ever economic hit
byline: Iran said on Friday that its response to any new U.S. threats would be ’’devastating’’ after Washington pledged to ​impose the toughest financial penalties in history with the aim of toppling the Iranian leadership.

title: SLPP files petition against 22nd amendment
byline: General Secretary of the Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) Attorney-at-Law Sagara Kariyawasam today filed a Special Determination petition before the Supreme Court challenging the constitutionality of the Bill titled “Twenty-Second Amendment to the Constitution,” which proposes to increase the retirement age of Supreme Court judges to 67 and Court of Appeal judges to 65.

title: Sri Lankan rescuers win long-term Korean visas
byline: Four years ago, three Sri Lankan migrant workers aboard a fishing boat off South Korea’s western coast spotted two Air Force pilots in the Yellow Sea after their fighter jet caught fire and crashed.

title: Charter plane crashes in Western Alaska, killing all 8 on board
byline: A charter plane crashed near a remote radar site in western Alaska, killing all 8 people on board, federal aviation and military officials said.

title: Temporary procedure introduced for Police clearance report
byline: The Sri Lanka Police has introduced a temporary procedure for Police Clearance Report applications following an unexpected technical failure affecting the computerized system of the Police Clearance Division.

title: Sri Lankan shooters return home with 10 medals from International Championships
byline: Sri Lanka’s national shooting team returned to the island after an impressive international campaign, winning a total of 10 medals — three gold, four silver and three bronze — at two major shooting championships held in Indonesia and the Philippines.

title: Hashan Tillakaratne appointed Sri Lanka batting coach
byline: Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) has appointed former Sri Lanka cricketer Hashan Tillakaratne as the Batting Coach of the Senior Men’s Program.

title: Japan hangs man convicted of killing 5 people in pachinko parlor fire
byline: A man who killed five people by setting fire to a pachinko parlor in 2009 was hanged Friday in Japan’s first execution by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s government, as the country faces growing calls for more transparency and the abolition of capital punishment.

title: Excessive lighting at temple festival in Jaffna leaves hundreds with vision problems
byline: Hundreds of people have reportedly experienced vision problems following the use of excessively bright electric lights as decorations at a temple in Jaffna.

title: Snake undergoes ’world-first’ human cancer therapy
byline: A snake named after the Hollywood star Jodie Foster has made a full recovery after receiving cancer treatment normally used in humans.

title: Heat warning issued for several areas
byline: The heat index, which reflects the temperature felt by the human body, is likely to increase to the ‘Caution’ level in parts of the Eastern Province and several districts during the daytime, the Meteorological Department said.

title: Police hunt three Chinese nationals in Port City murder case
byline: The Sri Lanka Police have appealed to the public for information to help locate three Chinese nationals wanted in connection with an alleged abduction and murder at Colombo Port City

title: Sri Lanka exports first fresh pineapple consignment to Pakistan
byline: Sri Lanka has exported its first consignment of fresh pineapples to Pakistan, opening a new overseas market for the country’s agricultural products.

title: Suresh Sallay’s wife urges President not to extend detention order
byline: The wife of former State Intelligence Service Director Maj. Gen. (Retd.) Suresh Sallay has made a fresh appeal to President Anura Kumara Dissanayake not to extend the detention order against her husband, citing what she described as a serious and potentially life-threatening cardiac condition.

title: Over 1,600 fatal road accidents reported so far this year
byline: A total of 1,654 fatal road accidents have been reported in Sri Lanka from the beginning of the year to yesterday (20), Deputy Inspector General of Police in charge of the Traffic Control and Road Safety Division W.P.J. Senadheera said.
